name: GE Power India Ltd
title: GE Power India Ltd - 532309 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Order book fell to INR 1,628 cr from INR 2,662 cr as FGD-EP contracts were terminated; core services orders up 32% and FY26 PBT of INR 340 cr is inflated by one-offs (BHEL ECL reversal ~INR 116 cr), with underlying EBITDA ~11%.

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 PBT from continuing operations hit INR 119 crore, but one-offs (incl. ~INR 44 crore BHEL ECL reversal) drove much of it; underlying FY26 EBITDA margin 11%.
summary.overview: GE Power India reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR 316 crore (up from INR 266 crore YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR 1,269 crore (up 21%), led by Core Services (+14%) and Upgrades (+24%). Profit before tax and exceptional items from continuing operations was INR 119 crore in Q4 versus a loss of INR 15 crore a year earlier, and INR 340 crore for FY26 versus INR 22 crore, with management flagging sizeable one-offs in both periods. Order intake fell sharply to INR 877 crore for FY26 from INR 2,183 crore, and order backlog declined to INR 1,628 crore from INR 2,662 crore, mainly due to termination of FGD-EP contracts. Management is pushing a service-led, short-cycle strategy, has settled with BHEL and Jaypee, and has signed a Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy, with a recommended dividend of INR 7 per share (70% of face value).

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% YoY and core orders rose 32% YoY; Core Services order backlog up about 40% YoY. Management says about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book executes in FY27 (12-month cycles).

segments.name: Upgrades
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 24% YoY, driven by upgrade volumes in Q4; Vindhyachal and Wanakbori complex upgrade orders of INR 591 crore were booked in FY25.

segments.name: New Build / FGD EPC (AQCS)
segments.commentary: In close-out mode; FGD-EP contracts of Jaypee Bina and Nigrie (INR 775 crore) were terminated, driving backlog decline. Seven operational acceptances and four unit completions achieved in FY26.

segments.name: Durgapur manufacturing (discontinued)
segments.commentary: Being demerged to JSW Energy; asset of about 660 acres, reported losses in recent quarters. Five-year JSW supply and capacity agreement signed to protect core services manufacturing needs.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numeric FY27 guidance; CFO said the FY26 underlying EBITDA base (11%) is set and FY27 margins should be at par or better, without a range.
About 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book (INR 1,628 crore) expected to execute in FY27, implying roughly INR 1,380-1,470 crore; this is a management estimate from the call, not formal guidance.
Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: filed with NCLT; target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest.
Core Services target addressable fleet of about INR 3,500-4,000 crore; company holds about 18% share and aims to grow it before considering other areas.
Management says the ECL impact from the BHEL settlement is fully recognised as of 31 Mar 2026, so no similar reversal is expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: Durgapur manufacturing facility to be demerged to JSW Energy; a five-year agreement with JSW covers reserved manufacturing capacity and supply for core services boiler components.
Management aims to build an alternate supply chain for boiler components within about 18 months to become independent of JSW after the five-year agreement.
Three PG tests completed for key new-build units and multiple synchronisations and facility closures achieved in FY26.
Eighteen new first-of-its-kind service products ordered during FY26; first-time generator repairs, turbine upgrades and control system solutions delivered.
demand_pricing: Management says thermal plant PLF and availability are rising, increasing services demand; target addressable market quoted at INR 3,500-4,000 crore.
Q4 order intake of INR 254 crore was below the prior-year INR 285 crore (which included INR 52 crore O&M); FY26 orders fell 60% YoY on the FY25 FGD-EP and complex upgrade wins.

FGD mandate: per the July 2025 notification, Category C plants (over 200 GW) were removed and Category A (about 8 GW, mainly Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra) must install FGD; Category B is optional with no tariff pass-through if they opt in. Management says the mandate has limited near-term order impact.
Management is pursuing 13 countries for boilers, including Vietnam, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Indonesia, while stating its perimeter remains India-only for GEPIL and non-GEPIL assets.

qa_highlights.question: Does GEPIL participate in gas turbine, HRSG or combined-cycle business?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said no; HRSG and gas-plant business belong to GE Vernova's gas business and fall outside GEPIL's objects, which are steam and thermal only.

qa_highlights.question: Of the order book, how much is executable in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Aashish Ghai said short-cycle orders typically complete within 12 months, so about 85-90% of the 31 Mar 2026 order book is expected in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will backlog grow after the current book runs off, and is the business widening beyond core?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is new-build close-out. Core backlog is up about 40% YoY; the company plans to grow its 18% share of the INR 3,500-4,000 crore fleet before expanding to other areas.

qa_highlights.question: What is the INR 450 crore loan and what yield does it earn?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said it is surplus cash lent to a promoter-group cash pool benchmarked to HSBC, with rates of 5.5-6.35% in FY26, about 0.25% above commercial bank deposit rates. Lending is board-approved, shareholder-approved and audited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the scope of the FGD opportunity and the margin range?
qa_highlights.answer: Roshan Singh outlined the notification: Category A (about 8 GW) must install FGD, Category B is optional, and Category C was removed. He said the mandate has limited weight for GEPIL unless utilities act proactively. No margin range was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for the INR 880 crore net cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Puneet Bhatla said the cash is under evaluation for deployment into growth in services, with no specific plan disclosed yet and shareholder value as the stated priority.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Durgapur demerger timeline and benefit to minority shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said the NCLT petition is filed, creditor and shareholder approvals and tax/bank NOCs are required, and completion is targeted for this calendar year and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders receive entitlement shares in the resulting company.

qa_highlights.question: Will the demerger affect manufacturing needed for core services?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no, because a five-year JSW Energy agreement reserves manufacturing capacity at pre-set schedule and price. An alternate supply chain is targeted within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying EBITDA margin excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said FY26 normalised entity-level EBITDA was 11%, with Q4 at about 18%. He declined to give a numeric margin range for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will ECL-related reversals continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Ghai said no; the BHEL settlement is fully executed, with the final tranche received in March 2026, and the ECL impact is complete as of 31 Mar 2026.

risks_watch: Order intake and backlog: FY26 orders INR 877 crore vs INR 2,183 crore; backlog INR 1,628 crore vs INR 2,662 crore. Watch whether Core Services orders keep rising as new-build backlog runs off.

Earnings quality: Q4 PBT of INR 119 crore and FY26 PBT of INR 340 crore include one-offs (BHEL ECL reversal of ~INR 116 crore for FY26, Solapur EoT/LD ~INR 22 crore, insurance ~INR 18 crore). Track the underlying 11% entity-level EBITDA margin in FY27.
Related-party exposure: INR 450 crore lent to the promoter-group cash pool (HSBC-benchmarked, 5.5-6.35% in FY26). Monitor the balance and whether it is recovered as cash is deployed.
Deployment of ~INR 880 crore net cash: no specific plan given; management only said it is under evaluation for services growth and shareholder value.

Durgapur demerger to JSW Energy: NCLT filing made; creditor, shareholder, tax and bank approvals pending. Target completion in calendar 2026, and within 12 months of 31 Mar 2026 at the latest. Also monitor the five-year JSW supply agreement and the 18-month alternate boiler supply chain.
key_quotes: So, what is declining is the new build orders backlog, which is the strategy of the company anyways, but what is increasing is the core orders backlog.
Now five years is a long period where we will then develop an alternate supply chain.
So, I can safely say that the base is set and, you know, the efforts it should be, you know, at par if not more at least but at least at par for the for the future years.
Our perimeter for the growth would be towards the focus area i.e. Services.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the service-led strategy, core order growth and the BHEL settlement closure, with the 70% dividend presented as a highlight. Evasive on forward numbers: no FY27 guidance beyond a 'base is set' margin comment, no range for the FGD opportunity, and no deployment plan for the INR 880 crore net cash.

adds.what: Durgapur manufacturing facility (~660 acres) being demerged to JSW Energy; reduces company's own manufacturing capacity
Alternate supply chain for boiler components (target ~18 months to become independent of JSW)

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management estimates 85-90% of the INR 1,628 crore backlog (about INR 1,380-1,470 crore) executes in FY27, with orders down 60% in FY26 (INR 877 crore) and Durgapur being demerged, so the outlook is flat-to-modest and only partly backed by the order book.
